lines: For every dollar a US online seller loses to fraud, the real cost is about five dollars.
Chargeback fraud is part of that bill.
scenes.visual: A closed case's file closing (records drop in, DEFEND lands) is on screen from frame one; for the first 2.6 s it sits blurred behind a scrim under the $5.13 stat (neutral source line; full citation in the video description).

lines: A PayPal dispute opens. A deadline starts.
It's easy to refund when you could have won, or to fight when the buyer is right.
scenes.visual: The $9.50 case on a phone (large, in a device frame) beside the same case on desktop: the deadline clock is visible.

lines: This is Dispute Defender.
It reads your PayPal disputes and shows what's at risk, and which deadline matters most.
scenes.visual: The case board (gentle push-in); the cursor moves to "Watch the agent work a case" and clicks it.

lines: One click, and the agent gets to work.
It reads the dispute, the order and the tracking from PayPal.
Every step reads PayPal's dispute APIs, recorded from the sandbox for this demo.
scenes.visual: From the moment the first record lands: records drop into the case file, claims tie to their records with drawn lines, and the DEFEND stamp lands.

lines: On this case, tracking shows delivery to the right ZIP code.
Claude drafts the response, and every claim links to its source.
The buyer wrote in Spanish, so the reply is in Spanish.
scenes.visual: Same case: the AI-written (recorded) response types in; the buyer wrote in Spanish, so the reply is Spanish with an English gloss.

lines: Tap a source to see the exact record behind a claim.
Nothing is invented. Our server checks every claim before you see it.
scenes.visual: The cursor taps a plain-language source chip; the matching record in the timeline highlights. Then the claims with their checkmarks.

lines: Before anything is sent, you see exactly what PayPal will receive.
The exact request, word for word.
scenes.visual: The cursor clicks "What PayPal receives": the exact POST endpoint and JSON body.

lines: Here the package is still on its way, and the case is for nine dollars fifty.
Fighting would cost more of your time than the refund.
So it says: refund. It tells you when a fight isn't worth it.
scenes.visual: The $9.50 case: the cursor clicks "Start the agent"; the REFUND stamp lands; the recommendation explains the cost to fight.

lines: You approve, and it goes through PayPal's dispute API.
Then you see the outcome. In the sandbox, this one was won.
scenes.visual: Band label "Earlier, on the $12.75 case" over its History row (POST …/send-message · 200); then Outcomes with the WON row highlighted while it's named.

bandLabels.text: Earlier, on the $12.75 case: a real sandbox submission

lines: Then it helps you prevent the next dispute.
Patterns across your cases, each with its evidence, and what to change.
scenes.visual: Insights: the first pattern (buyers open cases before delivery) and the suggested changes in focus.

lines: Under the hood: six PayPal APIs and an extended PayPal Agent Toolkit.
scenes.visual: Architecture card builds left → right (PayPal APIs, then the agent, then the honesty guarantees).

lines: Win the disputes worth fighting, and settle the rest fairly.
scenes.visual: Close card: the tagline, with one marker stroke on "fairly".

lines: Try the demo store, no login needed. Thanks for watching.
